agent_authored.description: Python port of the FV3 non-hydrostatic finite-volume dynamical core plus the SHiELD physics suite, run through the NDSL domain-specific layer (GT4Py + DaCe) so one source compiles to CPU and GPU. Integrates the atmosphere on a cubed-sphere grid: an inner acoustic sub-loop (C/D-grid shallow-water winds and a semi-implicit non-hydrostatic vertical solve), an outer loop (tracer transport and Lagrangian-to-Eulerian remapping), and physics parameterisations. Reference: Pace v0.2, Ben-Nasr et al., GMD 2023.

shared_components.title: Stencil DSL, grid setup and run harness
shared_components.purpose: The GT4Py/DaCe stencil DSL and its backends, the cubed-sphere grid metrics and analytic initialization that define the problem instance, run configuration, the FV3 driver and example decks, and the translate/savepoint test framework. This is the toolchain and scaffolding the dynamical core is written against and graded by; it is deliberately not part of the module, so a candidate optimizes the compute path and not the harness.

modules.title: FV3 non-hydrostatic dynamical core: the whole integration path per model time step
modules.expensive_path: One call to fv_dynamics per model time step drives everything this module owns. The acoustic sub-loop runs n_split times inside that step: each iteration does the C-grid advective half step, the D-grid full step with divergence damping and del2/del4 diffusion, the column-serial non-hydrostatic Riemann solve, and the halo exchanges that stitch the six cubed-sphere tiles together. After the sub-loop the step transports every tracer with the PPM finite-volume scheme, then remaps the deformed Lagrangian layers back to the fixed Eulerian coordinate and runs the moist adjustment. Wall time is dominated by the horizontal stencil sweeps in the acoustic sub-loop and by halo-exchange latency at higher rank counts; the vertical solves are column-serial and parallelise across columns but not within a column.
modules.rationale: The dynamical core is one unit of work, not five. The earlier five-way cut split a single closed loop into pieces that each owned a handful of stencil files while the grid, DSL, state containers and stencil helpers they all depended on stayed in a shared component larger than every module combined, so each piece was thin and none of them could be optimized without reaching across the boundary. Cutting it once, at the dycore boundary, makes the ownership match the physics: fv_dynamics and everything it calls per time step is owned, the toolchain that compiles it and the grid that defines the problem stay shared, and the module is measured end to end on a full model step rather than on four stencils in isolation. It also removes the overlap the earlier cut could not avoid, where dyn_core imported the Riemann solver and embedded halo updates that belonged to two other modules.
excluded: The GT4Py/DaCe stencil DSL (NDSL/ndsl/dsl/): this is the compiler and backend layer the module is written against, not the science it computes. A candidate retunes stencils and data movement; it does not rewrite the toolchain.
Grid metrics and analytic initialization (NDSL/ndsl/grid/, pyFV3/pyfv3/initialization/): these define the problem instance, so they must stay fixed for a result to be comparable.
The driver, run configuration and example decks (pace/, pyFV3/pyfv3/_config.py, examples/configs/): harness, not compute path.
The translate/savepoint test framework (NDSL/ndsl/stencils/testing/, pyFV3/pyfv3/testing/): test infrastructure that must stay fixed to keep the checks honest.
pySHiELD physics in its entirety: it does not import at this pin (see the not_packaged entry).
hazards: The cubed sphere has eight corner cells where the stencil is undefined and is patched by copy_corners and NDSL corners.py; a reimplementation that skips the corner treatment matches in the interior and is wrong at the seams.
Halo-exchange correctness is exact equality of the halo region, not a tolerance: an off-by-one in the rotation or buffer packing shows up only at tile edges, and only on multi-rank layouts.

The vertical solves (Riemann, remapping) are column-serial tridiagonal recursions. They parallelise across columns but not within a column, so a naive GPU port of this module can slow down on exactly these kernels.
The moist adjustment uses phase-partition thresholds rather than smooth functions, so small perturbations can flip a cell between phases and produce a large, legitimate output difference.
Pace already ships GT4Py and DaCe GPU backends (orch:dace:gpu). A task on this module must be framed so a candidate cannot satisfy it by selecting an existing backend.

The sharpest per-kernel evidence is the 38 savepoint translate tests, which need an external serialized-Fortran corpus that this snapshot does not ship; without it the module is graded on the example decks and the CPU-runnable component suites.
modules.purpose: One call to fv_dynamics advances the atmosphere by one model time step, and everything this module owns runs inside that call. The acoustic sub-loop iterates n_split times over the C-grid half step, the D-grid full step with divergence damping and diffusion, the column-serial non-hydrostatic Riemann solve, and the halo exchanges that join the six cubed-sphere tiles. The outer step then transports every tracer with the PPM finite-volume scheme and remaps the deformed Lagrangian layers back onto the fixed Eulerian coordinate, finishing with the moist adjustment. These pieces share the same state arrays, the same halo machinery and the same stencil helpers, and upstream calls them from one place, so they are one unit of work rather than several.
primary_inputs: D-grid and C-grid winds (u, v, uc, vc)
layer pressure thickness delp and surface pressure
potential temperature pt and the non-hydrostatic vertical velocity w
tracer mixing ratios (water species and any passive tracers)
grid metrics and the cubed-sphere tile decomposition
run configuration: time step, n_split, damping coefficients, tracer count
primary_outputs: the full prognostic state advanced by one model time step
remapped Eulerian layers with conserved total energy and total water
tracer fields after PPM transport and the positivity fixers
exchanged halo regions consistent across all six tiles
algorithm_stages: acoustic sub-loop, n_split iterations: C-grid advective half step (c_sw)
acoustic sub-loop: D-grid shallow-water full step with vorticity and kinetic-energy fluxes (d_sw)
acoustic sub-loop: divergence damping and del2/del4 diffusion (divergence_damping, del2cubed, delnflux)
acoustic sub-loop: non-hydrostatic Riemann solve and pressure-gradient update (riem_solver3, sim1_solver, nh_p_grad)
acoustic sub-loop: Rayleigh friction (ray_fast) and cubed-sphere halo exchange
outer step: PPM tracer transport with positivity fixers (tracer_2d_1l, fvtp2d, xppm, yppm, fillz, neg_adj3)
outer step: Lagrangian-to-Eulerian vertical remapping (remapping, map_single, remap_profile)
outer step: moist adjustment and sub-grid mixing (saturation_adjustment, moist_cv, fv_subgridz)
unique_responsibilities: advancing the atmospheric state by one model time step on the cubed sphere
all halo exchange, edge rotation and buffer packing between the six tiles
the memory layout and halo-aware storage the stencils operate on
not_responsible_for: The GT4Py/DaCe stencil DSL and its backends, which compile this module but are not part of it
Grid metrics and analytic initialization, which define the problem instance and stay fixed
The driver, run configuration and example decks, which set up and launch a run
The translate/savepoint test framework, which grades the module and must stay fixed
pySHiELD physics, which does not import at this pin
modules.differences: The single unit of work in this codebase: one model time step end to end, owning the horizontal stencil sweeps, the column-serial vertical solves and the halo exchange that couples them, and measured on a full step rather than on individual stencils.

not_packaged.what: pySHiELD/ in its entirety: microphysics, radiation, PBL turbulence, shallow convection and surface schemes
not_packaged.why: The submodule does not import at this pin. All seven physics test modules fail collection with ImportError: cannot import name 'NullComm' from 'ndsl', because the pySHiELD pin lags an NDSL API change. This is the most valuable unclaimed part of the codebase (radiation and microphysics are the classic physics-acceleration targets) and it should be revisited on a pin where pySHiELD imports.

The stencil compiler and orchestration layer. Accelerating the compiler is a compiler engineering task, not a scientific computing one, and the two external packages are third-party public projects rather than part of this codebase.
Grid metric generation and analytic initialisation run once at startup rather than per time step. Listed as shared infrastructure: every module needs the grid, and no module should own it.
Output, checkpointing and plotting. Their correctness question is I/O fidelity rather than physics.

Genuinely expensive stencil helpers, but each is called from two or more of the modules above. Assigning one to a single module would break the self-contained check rule; they are shared infrastructure and are exercised through whichever module calls them.

known_review_gaps.what: NDSL external/gt4py and external/dace pins dropped while setup.py installs them from those local directory paths; the pinned tree does not install as shipped.
known_review_gaps.resolution: Either vendor gt4py@511a7ab and dace@e432a8c (plus DaCe's nested cub/moodycamel/dace-webclient submodules; roughly doubles the payload and adds gt4py, dace and those nested submodules as new licence surfaces) or move to an NDSL pin whose setup.py resolves them from PyPI. Curator picks when this is taken up.

known_review_gaps.what: No recorded human curator approval of the module cut. The earlier five-module cut was sent back by the reviewer as too thin with heavy shared infrastructure; this revision replaces it with a single dynamical-core module, which the curator has not yet approved.
known_review_gaps.resolution: Presented as proposed-only. The curator approves this single-module cut in words at STOP 1, recorded with `codebase approve-modules --human-ref`, before anything downstream is scaffolded.

known_review_gaps.what: pySHiELD integration tests import NDSL NullComm, which the pinned NDSL no longer exports (LocalComm/MPIComm only); physics tests fail collection.
known_review_gaps.resolution: pySHiELD left not_packaged at this pin; revisit on a pin where pySHiELD imports.

known_review_gaps.what: The sharpest per-kernel evidence is the 38 savepoint translate tests, which need an external serialized-Fortran corpus that this snapshot does not ship.
known_review_gaps.resolution: Without that corpus the module is graded on the example decks and the CPU-runnable component suites; the curator accepts that evidence base or asks for a data plan at STOP 1. The module-overlap half of this gap is resolved by the single-module cut.

known_review_gaps.what: Pace already ships GT4Py/DaCe GPU backends (orch:dace:gpu default), so a naive port task could collapse to backend selection.
known_review_gaps.resolution: Curator judges whether the eventual task is a real optimization/port; not decided by this source review.
